x: This is the leg where the race can be won and lost, and names such as Hyman (who produced a fantastic new record - 34 seconds better than his own previous best), Wilkinson, Perry, North, Reed, Edmonds, Hogan and Foord appeared - enough to frighten the stoutest of hearts.

STAGE VIII - Ron Linstead (30:51 15th fastest) Ron could hardly have picked a tougher task than dealing first with Gerry North, who put up the fastest time of the day on this leg,and then Hogan of Polytechnic who both swept past in quick succession.
Gerry North then took over for the penultimate stage and showed everyone what a great road-runner he is by smashing Hogan's course record by 9 seconds, to record a fantastic 12:38.

On Whit Monday, he was 2nd to Hogan in the Inter-Counties '6' with a time of 28:37.2 and on July 5th he ran in the Helsinki World Games, finishing second to Vaillant (France) in the 10,000 m with 30:13.4.
Bill Kerr, who caught and passed Poly's front-running Irishman, Hogan, at half-way, won in a fine 8:51. Gerry North (9:01) was 3rd, Tony Fairclough (9:28) 8th and Laurie O'Hara (9:31) 10th.
Nevertheless he gained one place and finished at Purley close up to all but the leaders who were now Polytechnic--Hogan having put up a great performance for them with fastest time of the day.
'B' team times:- Biscoe 20:01, Satchell 22:51, Crookes 19:57, Mead 22:44 Shippen 20:04, Keavey 20:28, Bromley 19:43. Fastest times:-Batty (Thurrock) 16:48, Hogan(Poly)17:09,Baldwin(B/Heath)17:23

Assuming that all users of Arthur's cottage are paid up members of this second-claim "club" then there must have been some pride in achieving National placings of 4th (Hogan), 5th (Johnstone), 8th (R.
Following up are Cox, Adcocks, Turner, Moxom, Ashton, D. Holt and Hogan.

With the rhythm set, Johnstone, Grove, Holt (R) and Hogan took 2-lap stints in front to tow the field through 3 miles in 13:44.2. Only 3 seconds covered the first 16 at this point with Gerry still in the bunch, but not looking quite so frisky now.
…here he also passed Mitcham's Kortenray, and Nulholland of Hercules Wimbledon. The lead was now held by Walton, through Hogan.…
